A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PID Steering work. All 31 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including appendices A-C, provide readable, matchable text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: Sections 5.1-5.3, Tables 1-3 and the figures report original toxicity mitigation, jailbreaking, image-steering and controller-dynamics results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds controller-gain sweeps and evaluations of larger and deeper-safety-aligned Gemma models.

M1.justification: Section 3.2, Definition 1 and Equations 14-18 retain the same PID steering law and sequential/non-sequential direction construction. The additional analyses do not introduce an algorithmic component or change the steering procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain RealToxicityPrompts, AdvBench/Alpaca, Wikipedia, MMLU/TinyBenchmarks and COCO-based cyberpunk/steampunk style control. The additional Gemma checkpoints are model configurations within retained tasks; no new evaluation data or input conditions are documented.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ActADD, CAA, AURA and ITI-C for both toxicity models, substantially broadening comparisons beyond Original and Mean-AcT/Linear-AcT variants. The jailbreak comparator set remains unchanged, including in the added model evaluations.

E3.justification: v2 adds QVQ-72B-Preview judging, Gemma2-27B and deeper-safety-aligned Gemma2-9B evaluations, and systematic Kp/Ki/Kd sweeps with multiple evaluators in Figure 6. These substantially expand the evaluation design. Previously stated splits, prompt counts and image-generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained P/PI/PID trajectory comparisons, Section 5.4 and Figure 6 add sensitivity analyses of controller gains and their interactions on toxicity and jailbreaking. Appendix C.2 adds a robustness comparison against deeper safety alignment. Existing trajectory and image-style analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions retain ten-run averaging. However, v2 removes the reported uncertainty values from Gemma's Original utility metrics and all five previously reported Llama Original metrics. Other methods retain the existing mean-plus/minus reporting practice; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline and QVQ scores, gain-response heatmaps, and two model-result blocks. For the new deeper-aligned Gemma model, PID reports 34.75% ASR versus ITI's 23.12%. Table 1 revises Original classifier toxicity from 4.13 to 4.17 and 5.30 to 5.80. Existing PID toxicity scores and all retained Table 3 numerical rows remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.8 incorporates nonlinear Taylor remainders into the disturbance and derives residual-perturbation expressions under P/PI/PID, discussing boundedness conditions for extending the stability arguments. v2 also corrects the Taylor-expansion error sign in B.3 and changes P(k) to P(k+1) in the Lyapunov inequality in B.7.1. Core theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: interpreting existing steering as P control, introducing PID steering, reducing steady-state error and overshoot, and improving behavioral control across applications. Added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.8 adds nonlinear and strong-steering applicability arguments; C.3 adds a finite-depth rationale for balancing convergence speed and overshoot without claiming formal optimality. Section 5.1 replaces strong utility-preservation assertions with comparisons acknowledging AcT-related losses. Section 5.4 newly interprets the gain sweeps as evidence of architecture-independent controller behavior.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code location in the abstract; v1 only states that code accompanies supplementary materials. Figure 6 identifies LlamaGuard3 as the ASR evaluator and discloses tested gain values. New acknowledgments identify FPT AI Factory GPU access. The PDFs alone do not verify the linked code's availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Edwards et al. on time-varying stability, PIDformer, Teo et al., deeper safety alignment, QVQ and Vaswani et al., while removing Dang et al. Appendix A's related-work discussion and principal positioning remain unchanged. Several other citation changes only update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the Figure 3 explanation and revise toxicity and image-result prose. v2 adds analysis subsections and acknowledgments and changes author ordering, affiliations and the publication header. The main section sequence, method exposition and conclusion remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the twelve-heatmap Figure 6, expands Table 1 from six to ten rows per model with a QVQ column, and adds model blocks to Tables 2 and 3. These substantially expand the experimental displays. Existing diagrams, trajectory plots and image grids are retained, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Broader toxicity comparisons, a second judge, gain-sensitivity evidence and the deeper-safety test make the empirical assessment more informative. The qualified utility discussion, mathematical corrections and explicit code location also help. These gains are limited by removed Original-baseline uncertainties and Section 5.4's overstated interpretation of Figure 6: toxicity worsens at high integral gains rather than showing consistently improving or saturating behavior.
